questions.stem: According to the GenerateEmbedUrl API reference, which is true of the returned EmbedUrl?
options: Valid for the whole SessionLifetimeInMinutes and reusable
Contains a temporary bearer token, valid for 5 minutes, and cannot be re-used once redeemed
Valid for 24 hours for the same user
Only valid from the AWS console domain
questions.explanation: The URL is a short-lived, single-use bearer token. The session it opens lasts SessionLifetimeInMinutes (15 to 600, default 10 hours). So the backend mints a fresh URL per page load and nothing may cache it.

questions.stem: Tidewater embeds for tenants that do not have Quick Sight users and pay per session capacity. Which apply? Choose two.
options: GenerateEmbedUrlForAnonymousUser with AuthorizedResourceArns limited to the tenant's dashboards
SessionTags with the tenant id for tag-based RLS rules
A UserArn in the tenant's namespace
User-based RLS rules datasets keyed on user names
RegisterUser on every page load
questions.explanation: Anonymous embedding has no Quick Sight user; scope comes from AuthorizedResourceArns and session tags that tag-based RLS rules match. UserArn and user-based rules belong to registered embedding.

questions.stem: The portal moved to app.tidewater.example and partner portals live under many subdomains of portal.tidewater.example. What should AllowedDomains contain?
options: Every partner subdomain listed individually
https://app.tidewater.example and https://*.portal.tidewater.example
app.tidewater.example/ with a trailing slash
* to allow everything
questions.explanation: AllowedDomains overrides the console list for that call, accepts up to three domains or subdomains, and https://*.domain covers subdomains. Origins are scheme plus host, no path.

questions.stem: Registered embedding returns QuickSightUserNotFoundException for a new Corvid user. Best fix?
options: Switch Corvid to anonymous embedding
Provision the reader in Corvid's namespace (RegisterUser, e.g. on first login) and tell the admin when it is missing
Retry the call with backoff
Use the root user's ARN
questions.explanation: Registered embedding needs a Quick Sight user in the right namespace. Provision on first login or through an admin flow; retries will not create the user.

questions.stem: Which statements about SPICE are correct? Choose two.
options: SPICE is an in-memory engine that holds imported copies of data, consuming SPICE capacity
SPICE datasets can be refreshed on a schedule or through the API (ingestions)
Direct query and SPICE behave identically for freshness
SPICE removes the need for RLS
SPICE data is updated in real time from the source
questions.explanation: SPICE stores imported data and is refreshed on schedules or via CreateIngestion; direct query reads the source at query time. Imported data is not live and still needs RLS.

questions.stem: A dataset has a user-based RLS rules dataset keyed on tenant_id. A user in no rule row opens the dashboard. Which default behavior should you design for and test?
options: They see all rows
They see no rows unless rules grant access (deny by default), so a missing rule shows an empty dashboard
They get an error 500
RLS is skipped for readers
questions.explanation: With RLS applied, access is granted by rules; users without matching rules see no data. That is safe but shows up as an empty dashboard, a common support ticket after onboarding.

questions.stem: You promote a dashboard from the dev account to prod, where the data source has a different ARN. Which mechanism is designed for this?
options: Copy the analysis JSON by hand
Asset bundle export and import jobs with override parameters for the data source
Share the dashboard cross-account
Recreate it in the console
questions.explanation: StartAssetBundleExportJob and StartAssetBundleImportJob move dashboards with their dependencies; override parameters replace environment-specific values such as data source connection details.

questions.stem: Which belong in the backend that mints embed URLs? Choose two.
options: Verify the caller's JWT and map the user to a tenant from claims
Set cache-control: no-store on the response and never log the URL
Cache the URL per tenant for five minutes to save calls
Accept the tenant from a query parameter for flexibility
Return the URL in an HTTP redirect so it lands in proxy logs
questions.explanation: The URL is a bearer token: mint it per request for the verified tenant, keep it out of caches and logs.

questions.stem: Which tool lets a dashboard filter by a value chosen in a control, or passed from the embedding page?
options: Calculated field
Parameter bound to a control and used in a filter
SPICE refresh
Namespace
questions.explanation: Parameters hold values set by controls, URLs or the Embedding SDK and drive filters and calculations; calculated fields compute values; namespaces isolate users.

questions.stem: A common multi-tenant pattern for registered users in Quick Sight is:
options: One AWS account per user
One namespace per tenant, with users and groups in that namespace and assets shared to them
A separate Quick Sight subscription per dashboard
All tenants in the default namespace with one shared group
questions.explanation: Namespaces isolate users and groups per tenant inside one account; combined with RLS and asset permissions this is the standard registered multi-tenant setup.

questions.stem: The host page must apply a filter and listen for errors from the embedded dashboard. What does that?
options: The Quick Sight Embedding SDK in the page
A CloudFront function
An extra GenerateEmbedUrl call per filter change
An iframe without the SDK
questions.explanation: The Embedding SDK embeds dashboards, visuals or the console and exposes events, parameters and runtime filtering to the host page.

questions.stem: Users complain of being logged out of analytics after 15 minutes. Which are true? Choose two.
options: SessionLifetimeInMinutes sets how long the embedded session lasts, from 15 to 600 minutes
A security decision to use 15 minutes is valid; the fix is a product decision, not a bug fix
The 5-minute URL validity is what logs users out
AllowedDomains controls session length
It means the URL was cached
questions.explanation: Session length is the SessionLifetimeInMinutes setting; the 5-minute limit applies to redeeming the URL, not to the session.
